correctness.rationale: The commuting criterion was derived directly from Brandt multiplication. The adjacency operator was reconstructed entrywise and decomposed into invariant subspaces whose dimensions sum to \(n^2\). Each block action was checked symbolically: the \(I,J\) block gives the first quadratic; the \(D_u,P_u\) blocks give the second quadratic; \(Q_u\) has eigenvalue \(n-2\); skew row-sum-zero matrices have eigenvalue \(-2\); symmetric zero-diagonal row-sum-zero matrices have eigenvalue \(0\). Exact rational replay for \(3\le n\le8\) verifies the identities, dimensions, and direct-sum rank. The finite replay is supporting evidence only; the statement for all \(n\ge3\) follows from the displayed algebraic decomposition.

It gives the adjacency/neighborhood structure but no spectral formula. A broader Rees-matrix commuting-graph paper was also checked and did not yield a covering spectral statement. Semantic database searches under exact and equivalent formulations returned only unrelated spectral results. The current and prior own ledgers were checked for recoverable claims and IDs; no prior Brandt commuting-graph spectral claim was found.
residual_risks: Spectral graph literature is broad and a non-indexed source could in principle contain an equivalent formula. This risk is reduced by direct inspection of the exact-object 2020 paper, the broader 2025 Rees-matrix paper, and exact/equivalent-form database searches.

value.rationale: The exact-object literature already treats many standard graph invariants for Brandt commuting graphs but leaves the adjacency spectrum unresolved in the inspected text. A closed spectrum is a natural structural invariant: it gives every eigenvalue and multiplicity uniformly, immediately determines adjacency singularity, and yields a closed energy formula. This is not a parameter substitution or finite table; it extracts a global invariant from a natural algebraic graph family.
